That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#2354. Bernard Vellut : « On veut que ce soit une belle fête »

À quelques jours du choc face à l’AS Saint-Étienne au Parc des Sports d’Annecy, pour le compte du 7e tour de la Coupe de France, le GFA Rumilly Vallières est en pleine effervescence. Le club haut-savoyard cultive un modèle unique porté par quatre co-présidents et un esprit résolument familial. L'un d'eux, Bernard Vellut (à droite sur la photo), revient pour nous sur les coulisses de cette ascension fulgurante, les défis structurels du club et l'excitation qui entoure la venue des Verts.

Bonjour Bernard Vellut et merci de nous accorder ces quelques minutes d’interview. Le club de Rumilly Vallières a la particularité d'être dirigé par quatre co-présidents avec chacun un rôle dédié. En ce qui te concerne, tu as en charge les instances de football et les collectivités territoriales. Comment est née cette organisation assez unique et comment vous répartissez-vous la charge au quotidien ?

Effectivement, nous sommes quatre co-présidents. Comment cela est-il arrivé ? Moi j'étais président du club de Rumilly et Luc Chabert était président du club de Vallières, à trois kilomètres de chez nous. On a donc évoqué un rapprochement de nos deux clubs, plutôt que de se tirer dans les pattes, sans parler encore de fusion. Mais il y avait toujours quelque chose qui clochait au niveau de détails plus ou moins importants. C'est toujours une question humaine de toute façon.

À un moment donné, on s’est dit qu'il fallait arrêter de se piquer les joueurs et réfléchir à faire quelque chose de plus grand. Avec Luc Chabert, qui a une très grosse entreprise de fromagerie avec une dizaine de laiteries, on s’est dit : « On y va ! ». On s’est donc réunis une fois, deux fois, trois fois. Au début ça tiquait un petit peu, mais on est arrivés à se dire qu'on allait commencer par tout le cursus jeunes. Les jeunes, eux, c'est d’abord la couleur du maillot, les histoires de personnes ils n’en ont rien à cirer ! On a fait deux années comme ça avec les jeunes et ça a tellement bien marché qu'on a ensuite souhaité fusionner tout le club. De là est née la structure des quatre co-présidents : j'avais un vice-président avec moi et Luc Chabert avait le sien de son côté. On s’est dit qu’on n’allait pas faire d'histoires et qu'à quatre co-présidents, on ne serait pas trop pour gérer le club.

Les choses se sont déroulées de la meilleure des façons. Au-delà de la présidence, on est tous devenus amis, ainsi que nos épouses respectives. Quand tu as quatre co-présidents comme ça qui mènent la barque, tous les gens derrière voient que ça marche super bien et l'engouement est parti. Au niveau de la répartition : Bruno Piccon s'occupe de toute la partie jeunes, Luc Chabert gère les partenaires, François Baudet s'occupe de la communication et du matériel, et pour ma part, je m'occupe des instances, des terrains, de la mairie de Vallières, du district, de la Ligue et de la Fédération. Je fais également partie du comité directeur de la Ligue où je représente les clubs nationaux de la région Rhône-Alpes, ainsi qu'au siège à Paris.

En dehors de cela, on a tous notre boulot, bien sûr. Toutes les trois semaines, on se réunit et on mange ensemble pour échanger sur les perspectives, les actions en cours ou à venir, et ce qui a été bien ou moins bien fait. Derrière, on a un comité directeur pour décider des orientations dans les différentes commissions, et trois semaines après, ces commissions nous rendent compte de leurs résultats. On avance comme ça, sans compter les coups de téléphone et les messages tous les deux jours... On communique beaucoup ! On est obligés de travailler comme cela maintenant parce qu'on a quand même 800 licenciés, ce n'est pas rien.

Comme tu le disais, le club est né d'une fusion en 2018, et il se retrouve aujourd'hui à une très belle place en championnat (le club est actuellement 2e de sa poule en National 1, à 3 points de Nîmes avec un match de retard, ndp²). Le club a aussi connu une épopée fantastique en Coupe de France en 2021. Quel regard portez-vous sur cette ascension fulgurante et est-ce que le monde professionnel est une ambition ou un doux rêve ?

On a l'habitude de faire les choses les unes après les autres. Quand on est montés, on voulait voir à quel niveau on pouvait se situer. Aujourd'hui, il ne faut pas se leurrer, les joueurs comme le staff sont pratiquement tous professionnels. Comme nous avons un budget serré, nous souhaitons avancer pas à pas et ne surtout pas brûler les étapes.

Au niveau du coach, nous avons un gars super, Cédric Rullier, qui a essentiellement recruté régionalement. On ne voulait pas recruter trop loin parce que la vie est très chère en Haute-Savoie et qu'il faut se loger. Maintenant qu'on a un niveau honnête avec de l’ambition, on va chercher un petit peu plus loin, mais toujours des joueurs ciblés sur leur mentalité et leur respect. C'est après les qualités sportives bien sûr, mais un joueur qui ne rentre pas dans notre moule mentalement, on ne le prend pas. On veut garder notre esprit familial, même si on s'est beaucoup professionnalisés.

On a énormément de bénévoles et on veut que la mayonnaise prenne entre eux et les joueurs. C'est ce qui fait notre force aujourd'hui : le groupe vit très bien, l'entraîneur est exceptionnel et les bénévoles sont hyper dévoués. Dès que tu demandes quelque chose, ils sont tous derrière toi pour t'aider. Aujourd'hui, c'est fantastique !

La Coupe de France, cela n’a rien à voir avec le championnat, les émotions sont multipliées par dix ou quinze. En 2021, lors de notre exploit, on a commencé en gagnant aux tirs au but contre un club de district, un truc de dingue. Petit à petit, on a passé les tours : on a sorti Prix-lès-Mézières et le FC Annecy aux tirs au but, puis Le Puy en huitièmes, Toulouse en quarts, avant de tomber contre Monaco en demi-finale. C'était complètement fou.

Le seul bémol, c'est que ça s'est joué pendant le Covid, donc il n'y avait pas de supporters au stade. Mais ça ne nous a pas empêchés de nous retrouver le soir des victoires. La mairie et la gendarmerie ont été très sympas avec nous parce qu'ils savaient qu'ils ne pouvaient pas faire autrement. J'ai une petite anecdote pour le match contre Monaco : le préfet avait donné l'autorisation à deux ou trois équipes de jeunes de nous accompagner à la sortie du restaurant à midi. Sauf qu'on s'est retrouvés à 3 000 dans les rues ! Les gendarmes n'ont rien pu faire, c'était un truc de fou. C'est une expérience qu'on ne reverra peut-être jamais, en tout cas pas moi, mais c'est tout le mal que je souhaite au club.

Depuis, ça fait trois ans qu'on se fait éliminer aux tirs au but. On s'était dit que cette année, il fallait que ça change pour aller chercher un 32e ou un gros club. On n'est pas encore en 32e, on a eu quelques soucis et on est encore passés aux tirs au but au tour précédent. J'ai l'impression que c'est dans la tête : quand tu rencontres une équipe plus faible, tu te mets à son diapason. Mais avec les joueurs qu'on a aujourd'hui, si on tombe contre une équipe plus forte, ils savent hausser leur niveau. On ne lâche rien. Par exemple, hier à Saint-Priest, il y avait 2-2 à un quart d'heure de la fin. On fait rentrer le banc, pouf, on met 4-2, et si le match continue on en met encore deux ou trois. C'est formidable.

Parlons un peu des infrastructures du club et de vos perspectives d'évolution. De quels terrains disposez-vous actuellement ?

On a un terrain en herbe à Rumilly avec un synthétique à côté. Le centre de Vallières est consacré aux jeunes et aux matchs de Ligue pour nos réserves (l'équipe 2 joue en R1 et l'équipe 3 en R3). Là-bas, on a un terrain en herbe et un synthétique tout neuf, deux jolis terrains.

Là où le bât blesse aujourd'hui, c'est à Rumilly : notre synthétique doit être refait et on voudrait améliorer le terrain en herbe. En ce moment il est beau parce qu'il pleut, mais l'été il est sec et l'hiver il gèle. Ce n'est pas une vraie pelouse de stade, elle a 50 ans. Les jardiniers s'en occupent très bien, mais il faut refaire la surface. On hésite entre synthétique, hybride ou herbe. On se bat un peu avec la mairie et la communauté de communes pour avoir une vision sur les prochaines années. Un beau terrain amène du beau jeu et des spectateurs, c'est un tout. Les municipalités ne sont pas contre, mais il faut trouver les fonds et les subventions.

Vous pouvez bénéficier d'aides financières des collectivités ?

Oui, la mairie nous donne 100 000 euros et la communauté de communes 100 000 euros aussi. Pour le département, les subventions dépendent de la division dans laquelle tu évolues. Avec la réforme des championnats et les changements d'appellation, on est en train de regarder à quoi on a droit en tant que premier niveau amateur de France. C'est un combat de tous les jours. Il faut rien lâcher, tout en gardant un bon état d'esprit et en évitant les conflits. Ça a déjà bien avancé par rapport à nos débuts, mais il en faut encore plus.

Quel est votre budget actuel et est-il stable ?

On est à 1,9 million d'euros. Quand on a fusionné, on était à 600 000 euros. Aujourd'hui, on doit avoir le dixième budget de notre poule. On est dans une poule Sud très relevée avec des clubs comme Nîmes ou Toulon. C'est quasiment une petite division supérieure, capable de rivaliser avec le milieu de tableau au-dessus.

Il y a aussi quatre clubs de la région lyonnaise dans votre groupe. Comment vous positionnez-vous face à eux, notamment sur le recrutement ?

Ils ont un gros avantage sur nous : ils ont des pépinières de joueurs partout, avec 20 ou 25 clubs au kilomètre carré. Nous, à part Annecy avec qui on travaille en partenariat, on est assez isolés. Lyon est à 120 kilomètres. Et puis à Rumilly, on est à côté d'Annecy et de Genève : un T2 coûte 800 ou 900 euros par mois, ce n'est pas 300 euros comme en Lozère ou dans le Centre. C'est pour ça qu'on fait très attention à qui on fait venir.

Justement, comment êtes-vous organisés pour recruter sans cellule de recrutement professionnelle ?

Nos deux coachs travaillent énormément à la vidéo et vont voir beaucoup de matchs. On a aussi un directeur sportif à plein temps et une petite cellule composée d'anciens joueurs du club. On les envoie observer des matchs à Mâcon, Bourg ou Thonon avec des fiches précises sur un joueur ciblé. On travaille aussi avec quelques agents qu'on connaît bien, même si ce n'est pas notre tasse de thé parce qu'un agent ne te dira jamais que son joueur est mauvais.

Avant de recruter un joueur, il est visionné trois ou quatre fois, en vidéo et en physique. Ensuite, le directeur sportif l'appelle pour sonder sa mentalité, et celle de sa compagne ou de sa famille, car c'est très important. On leur explique le coût de la vie ici. Niveau infrastructures, on est équipés avec salle de muscu et bains froids, mais on n'a pas des salaires de 4 000 euros comme dans le Midi. On ne veut pas qu'un gars arrive et dise qu'il ne peut pas vivre ici. Après, on se voit, on discute beaucoup avec Luc Chabert, le directeur sportif et les coachs. On marche au feeling, et en discutant avec la maman ou la copine, on voit vite si on ne se trompe pas sur la mentalité. En moyenne, entre la visio, les appels et les repas tous ensemble, on se voit plusieurs fois avant de signer. On prépare déjà la saison prochaine, en regardant plutôt vers le nord que vers le sud, car un joueur qui habite à Nîmes ou Hyères au bord de la mer avec un bon salaire est très dur à faire venir en Haute-Savoie.

Vous faites aussi monter des jeunes de votre réserve, j'imagine ?

Oui, mais on part de loin. Quand on a lancé la fusion chez les jeunes en 2016, le niveau n'était pas très élevé. Aujourd'hui, toutes nos équipes de U15, U17 et U18 évoluent en Régional 1. Notre équipe réserve, qui joue aussi en R1, est composée à 60 % de jeunes du club. Ils ne sont pas encore prêts pour briguer une place de titulaire en équipe première, mais chaque année, le coach en intègre quelques-uns. Cette saison, trois jeunes du club font tous les entraînements avec le groupe, et un ou deux sont vraiment prometteurs parce qu'ils haussent leur niveau.

C'est très dur d'atteindre le niveau national quand des gamins n'ont pas eu une grosse formation dès l'âge de 7 ou 8 ans. Maintenant, on commence à récolter les fruits de notre travail : ceux qu'on a pris à 7 ou 8 ans en ont 13 ou 14 aujourd'hui, et on voit qu'il y a un vrai niveau. Pour nous, faire monter des jeunes du club, c'est aussi l'avantage de ne pas avoir à leur chercher un appartement ! Mais en attendant, on recrute surtout des joueurs qui ont un bon niveau en National 2 et qui ont faim, plutôt que d'aller chercher des gars de Ligue 2 pour qui venir jouer chez nous serait vécu comme un échec.

Tu disais que les joueurs fonctionnent comme des pros. Ils vivent tous du football aujourd'hui ?

Statutairement on est amateurs, mais dans le fonctionnement, on est comme des pros. À part deux ou trois jeunes en service civique qui montent dans le groupe, tous les joueurs vivent de ça. Ils s'entraînent une à deux fois par jour. Comme les matchs ont souvent lieu le vendredi soir et qu'il faut partir dès le jeudi midi pour aller à Châteauroux ou ailleurs, il est impossible qu'ils travaillent à côté.

Sans entrer dans les détails indiscrets, quel est l'ordre d'idée des rémunérations ?

Je ne vais pas donner de chiffres précis. On fait des contrats d'un an, et on a deux ou trois joueurs qui sortent un peu du lot. Mais globalement, nos salaires sont 30 à 40 % moins élevés que dans les clubs du Midi. Ils en vivent, mais ce ne sont pas des salaires de cadres. Après, il n'y a pas que l'argent : les joueurs connaissent les conditions et le cadre de vie avant de signer. S'ils acceptent, ils savent où ils mettent les pieds et ça se passe très bien.

Un mot sur le vestiaire et le staff : vous avez notamment Cyril Martin-Pichon, formé à l'ASSE et qui a beaucoup joué dans les équipes de jeunes et même en réserve, qui est un cadre chez vous, et un staff très fidèle au club.

Oui, Cyril Martin-Pichon a quitté le système pro parce qu'il n'y adhérait plus tellement. Il pense au collectif et au plaisir avant tout. Ça fait trois ans qu'il est chez nous, c'est un excellent joueur avec une mentalité irréprochable, un vrai cadre.

Pour le staff, notre entraîneur Cédric Rullier est passé par Annecy, Chambéry et Lyon. Ça fait trois ou quatre ans qu'il est là. Il est diététicien à l'hôpital de Chambéry et, depuis l'an dernier, il a mis son métier entre parenthèses pour se consacrer uniquement au club. Tout le reste du staff est issu du club : son adjoint Damien Guerrier, notre jeune entraîneur des gardiens qu'on a formé, et nos deux préparateurs physiques. Ce ne sont pas des gens arrivés sur le tard, on les connaît depuis dix ans, depuis tout petits. Ils sont rémunérés par le club, sont exigeants — on améliore nos équipements chaque année — mais ils sont surtout dévoués à 100 %.

J'ai été impressionné par les statistiques de Rumilly cette année : vous avez une puissance de feu phénoménale en attaque ! Le nombre de buts que vous marquez est impressionnant.

C'est bizarre parce qu'en début de saison, on se disait justement qu'on était un peu courts en attaque ! Et finalement, on marque beaucoup de buts, je crois qu'on a la meilleure attaque de toutes les poules confondues. C'est grâce à notre force mentale et au coach qui tient bien son groupe. Les joueurs savent que si ça ne va pas, ils peuvent partir, mais à côté de ça, ils ont un cadre hyper convivial avec les bénévoles qui sont aux petits soins pour eux.

Il y a des joueurs qui se révèlent, comme Fortier qui avait dû marquer trois buts l'an dernier et qui est dans tous les bons coups cette saison. Et puis on a des gars très techniques au milieu comme Cyril Martin-Pichon, Yoann Martelat ou Quentin Foulay, qui donnent d'excellents ballons devant. J'espère que ça va durer.

Dans votre championnat, il n'y a que le premier qui monte, ou le deuxième joue des barrages ?

Il n'y a que le premier qui monte, il n'y a pas de barrages pour le deuxième. Après, comme chaque année avec les passages devant la DNCG, il arrive parfois que des places se libèrent et que le meilleur deuxième des trois poules soit repêché.

Et la Ligue 3 professionnelle, si l'occasion se présente, vous y pensez ?

Comme je le disais au départ, ce sont les résultats qui décideront. L'an dernier déjà, à la trêve, on était premiers et on commençait à se poser la question. Sportivement, on peut y arriver si les joueurs le méritent. Mais aujourd'hui, je trouve que la Ligue 3 n'est pas encore prête au niveau de la Fédération, et les aides financières ne sont pas forcément à la hauteur de ce qui avait été annoncé.

Un bon copain qui est au Puy m'a prévenu que le cahier des charges est énorme : il faut des caméras, des parcages visiteurs, un directeur de club. Si tu ne remplis pas tous les critères, on te retient des pénalités sur les subventions, et sur les 300 000 euros prévus, il ne t'en reste plus que 150 000 à l'arrivée. Les déplacements ne seraient pas un problème puisqu'on traverse déjà toute la France, mais il faudrait vraiment de grosses aides du département, de la mairie et de la communauté de communes pour mettre le stade aux normes.

Revenons à la Coupe de France. Quelle a été la première réaction au club quand le tirage au sort a désigné l'AS Saint-Étienne ?

Moi, j'étais à Paris pour le tirage. Trois journalistes m'ont sauté dessus avant même la fin pour me demander ce que j'en pensais et où on allait jouer ! Ce n'est pas un soulagement, c'est l'opportunité qu'on cherchait : tomber sur un club pro dès le 7e tour.

La question du stade s'est tout de suite posée parce qu'à Rumilly, on a une capacité de 2 500 places, impossible d'accueillir les Verts. Sébastien Faraglia, le président du FC Annecy, m'a tout de suite appelé pour nous dépanner. C'est un ami, je l'ai connu joueur et entraîneur à Rumilly, et Luc Chabert est aussi partenaire du FC Annecy avec ses entreprises. Il y a une vraie osmose.

Au club, ça a été l'embrasement général, tout le monde ne parlait que de ça alors qu'on avait deux matchs de championnat à jouer entre-temps. L'entraîneur a très bien géré le coup. Dès le lundi après le tirage, il a enfermé les joueurs dans le vestiaire et leur a dit : « Le premier qui parle de Saint-Étienne ou qui s'économise, avec moi ça ne marchera pas ». Résultat, on a gagné 5-0 contre Istres et 4-2 hier. Maintenant, on peut se consacrer à Saint-Étienne.

Comment abordez-vous ce match face à un monument du foot français ?

Il y a deux divisions d'écart, ce sont des pros, et Saint-Étienne est un club que tout le monde adore. Après, c'est la trêve internationale, donc ils ont pas mal de joueurs partis en sélection. Il restera une très belle équipe, on ne va pas se cacher, mais ce ne sera pas l'équipe type. En coupe, les niveaux se resserrent et les équipes inférieures haussent souvent le ton. D'habitude, on dit que le terrain avantage le petit, mais là on jouera sur la pelouse hybride d'Annecy, l'une des meilleures de France. Au niveau technique et du jeu, ça va vraiment être le top.

Le Parc des Sports d'Annecy sera à guichets fermés ?

Pas encore. Saint-Étienne a eu une ouverture prioritaire pour ses Ultras — il y aura d'ailleurs deux groupes d'Ultras de Saint Etienne qui feront le déplacement. La billetterie grand public a ouvert depuis avant-hier. Le stade fait 13 000 places, mais la jauge de sécurité sera fixée autour de 10 000 ou 10 500 spectateurs. Pour des raisons de sécurité, les spectateurs en tribune ne peuvent pas croiser le parcage stéphanois pour aller aux toilettes, donc on doit condamner un quart de virage, ce qui enlève environ 2 000 places.

On a vendu entre 5 000 et 6 500 places les deux ou trois premiers jours, et là on tourne à 100 ou 150 billets par jour. S'il fait beau dimanche, tous les papas avec leurs enfants vont se dire qu'ils prennent une place à 10 euros pour voir le match. S'il pleut, ils viendront moins. Ils annoncent un petit peu de pluie, on verra bien.

Vous sentez toute la région derrière vous ?

Oui, on sent que les Verts arrivent à Annecy. Bon, les Annéciens sont un peu habitués puisqu'ils les jouent en championnat. Ici, les gens ne parlent même pas de notre équipe, ils parlent des Verts qui débarquent ! C'est un club emblématique, historique, c'est comme ça. Quant à nos joueurs, je les ai vus hier soir : ils sont confiants, dans leur bulle. Ils pensent à Saint-Étienne mais n'en font pas une maladie, pour ne pas jouer le match trois fois dans leur tête avant dimanche. Mais à partir d'aujourd'hui, ça va forcément commencer à trotter.

Si tu devais signer tout de suite pour un scénario de match — même une qualification stéphanoise à l'arraché après une rencontre dantesque — qu'est-ce qui te ferait dire que l'événement est une réussite totale ?

L'événement sera une réussite à partir du moment où le stade sera plein. Enfin, il sera plein, j’en suis sûr ! Ensuite, il faut qu'on fasse un match à la hauteur de notre niveau. Même si on perd, si c'est un beau match, les gens seront contents : ils auront vu une belle équipe de Saint-Étienne et ils auront vu qu'on a su répondre présent. Ce sera une fête réussie, en espérant derrière que ça nous laisse quand même un petit reliquat financier. On aura fait notre boulot face aux Verts.

Saint-Étienne devrait vous laisser sa part de la recette, normalement ?

On verra. Je pense que si on accueille bien les spectateurs, si on fait une belle fête, si les supporters — parce que ce sont eux qui font l'ambiance — sont bien reçus et qu'il n'y a pas de problème avec l'équipe de Saint-Étienne, ils la laisseront. Ils nous ont demandé plein de choses au niveau des vestiaires, mais si tout se passe bien, il n'y aura pas de souci. De toute façon, ce n'est pas dans notre habitude de recevoir des équipes en se disant qu'on va les matraquer. Quand on a reçu Monaco, ils avaient fait notre éloge pour l'accueil, parce qu'on n'avait pas joué pour blesser ou pour détruire. Ce sera exactement dans la même lignée : on n'est pas là pour casser du Vert, loin de là, au contraire, on est là pour profiter. Par contre, si on a l'occasion de passer, on passera, c'est sûr !

Tu parlais des demandes de Saint-Étienne pour les vestiaires, ils ont beaucoup d'exigences ?

Ça ne m'a pas trop surpris. Comme notre coach est diététicien, quand on se déplace, on a déjà pas mal de choses : différentes eaux, des minéraux, des barres de chocolat, des casse-croûtes, des tapis, des biscuits... Là, c'est dans le même style, en amplifié : de l'eau, des barres de céréales, des fruits, etc. C'est assez énorme, mais ça ne nous surprend pas parce qu'on fait déjà un peu la même chose.

Qui sont vos interlocuteurs au sein du club de Saint-Étienne pour organiser tout ça ?

Quand j'étais à Paris pour le tirage, un ancien joueur de Saint-Étienne qui fait partie de l'encadrement m'a contacté en me disant que le directeur allait m'appeler, et cinq minutes après, il m'appelait. On est en contact avec le directeur du club (Jean-François Soucasse, NDLR) et le directeur de la sécurité. Les relations ont été très sympathiques avec des gens très gentils. Nous avons de très bons rapports.

Une dernière question : est-ce que tu serais d’accord pour que l'année prochaine,  peut-être à la même époque, on refasse un petit point pour voir un peu où vous en êtes un an après avoir joué les Verts ?

Oui, il n'y a pas de souci. Ce sera avec plaisir.

Eh bien écoute Bernard, un grand merci pour ton temps, bonne journée et bon match pour dimanche !

L'ASSE et la Coupe d'Europe, cela a longtemps été une histoire compliquée. Les années 60 étaient souvent celles du blues pour les Verts...

#2353. Sports club members becoming less tolerant of homosexuality

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.

The organisation found that 66% of people had no objection to a fellow member of a sports club being gay, while in 2008 the figure was 85%.

Just over half (55%) of respondents said they had no problem sharing a shower with a gay team-mate of the same sex, which also represented a drop from 73% in 2008.

The Mulier Institute said the findings reflected a social trend that has also been seen in schools, where the proportion of boys aged between 12 and 16 with a positive view of homosexuality has dropped from 40% to 22% since 2021.

The Dutch Olympic Committee NOC*NSF said the findings were “highly regrettable” and pledged to step up its efforts to make sport more inclusive.

But the John Blankenstein Foundation, which campaigns for LGBT emancipation in sport, said it had noticed declining enthusiasm for its workshops and growing numbers of parents who voiced objections.

Karin Blankenstein, who set up the organisation in 2008, told NOS: “I get the sensitivity around transgender people in sport at the top level, but this is about amateur sport.”

#2350. Cathro veut faire plaisir au petit Ian

Tout en ayant confirmé les absences de Larso, Svetlin, Eymard et Dhaoui (blessé hier à l’entraînement) et la titularisation de Lavallée dans les cages (« il travaille beaucoup, il est très sérieux, il est prêt »), Ian Cathro a donné, avec son habituelle détermination sa vision de ce premier tour de Coupe de France, dimanche face à Rumilly-Vallières (15h) :

"Les jeunes joueurs vont avoir l’opportunité de se montrer. On a besoin d’eux. Mais pour moi ce qui est important, c’est de mériter ce maillot. On est très attentif à leurs entrainements, à leurs matchs, on a un dialogue quasi quotidien avec le staff. On essaye de construire quelque chose qui permettra d’écrire le prochain chapitre de ce club, c’est au-delà de 34 matchs, au-delà des prochaines semaines. On essaye de travailler en intégrant tout le monde pour que le prochain chapitre de ce club soit plus sain et plus performant que les précédentes années.

Mais je veux ajouter que je préfèrerais ne pas jouer de match officiel pendant une trêve internationale. On accorde la même importance à chaque match. On espère gagner ce match et avancer en Coupe de France, et on joue avec le sentiment de responsabilité, et la pression de la gagne, et c’est une sensation étrange de faire ça durant une trêve internationale sans avoir tout le monde de disponible. Mais c’est notre réalité du moment, alors on y va ! Il faut gagner le prochain match, respecter toutes les compétitions, et donc gagner le prochain match. On sait où on est, ce qu’on veut être, ce qu’on représente. On respecte l’histoire de ce club, qui est le 3e au nombre de victoires dans cette compétition. Donc évidemment, je ne peux que vous dire qu’on espère gagner chaque match. Si on gagne chaque match, on gagnera le Championnat et la Coupe. Mais c’est très difficile. C'est la façon dont on vit, dont on travaille, chaque jour, en essayant de progresser. On est obsédé par l’idée de progresser chaque jour pour décrocher la victoire.

Quand j’étais un petit garçon, et que je suis tombé amoureux du foot, j’ai toujours senti que la Coupe était une compétition spéciale, parce que c’est souvent le dernier match de la saison, la finale, la télé en parle toute la journée, c’est un jour très spécial. Je suis toujours ce petit garçon qui adore le foot et parfois il y a plus de magie, plus d’émotion avec cette Coupe qu’avec la routine hebdomadaire du championnat. Oui c’est différent, c’est spécial, il y a toujours des histoires qui font l’Histoire, et j’aimerais qu’on en écrive une partie. Pour cela il faut travailler, et chercher chaque jour à progresser."

#2349. Bayern set for crunch talks with Neuer over his future

Manuel Neuer is widely expected to retire at the end of the season, with Sky Germany going as far as to report that there is a “99.9 percent” chance he will hang up his gloves when his contract with Bayern Munich expires in the summer of 2027.

However, the 40-year-old has yet to clearly communicate whether he intends to call time on his career at the end of the season.

According to Kicker, Bayern are keen to clarify the situation and are therefore planning to sit down with Neuer to discuss his future during the international break.

Should Neuer retire as expected, Jonas Urbig is in line to become Bayern's new first-choice goalkeeper, while the club could bring in an experienced shot-stopper as his backup. Hoffenheim's Oliver Baumann, Fulham's Bernd Leno and Schalke 04's Loris Karius have all been mentioned as potential options.

Neuer is currently sidelined with a foot injury that is expected to keep him out for the remainder of the year.

#2347. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

The teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly new rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

This is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

Some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. Lucas Digne has only just swapped Aston Villa for PSG in recent days but he already comes up against his old teammates. He is on the bench for PSG tonight and could offer some good insight into Unai Emery’s side.

PSG forwards Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and both are on the bench for PSG tonight. As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days? Team news is in 🔒 #PSGAVL pic.twitter.com/yeKkyIKiHQ

What will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he said. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

Excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop said the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

#2340. Bayern chief reveals Guardiola had Kompany on three-man shortlist to replace him at Man City

It has previously been revealed that Bayern Munich contacted Pep Guardiola before appointing Vincent Kompany as head coach in 2024 to hear the then-Manchester City manager's thoughts on the Belgian.

Guardiola knew Kompany from his time as a player and captain at Manchester City and had also faced him as a fellow manager in England, where Kompany was in charge of Burnley before being relieved of his duties.

The Catalan coach clearly thought highly of the former Belgium international. In fact, as Bayern supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has now revealed, Guardiola even considered Kompany one of the top three candidates to succeed him at Manchester City at the time.

“We thought we’d hear what Pep had to say before making our final decision. So I called him,” Rummenigge told Bundesliga.com.

"We had a long conversation, lasting an hour and a half. Pep had nothing but praise for him. At some point, I asked him to give me an authentic, honest answer. He told me that he had a shortlist. Manchester City had asked him to put one together in case he ever decided to leave, and Vincent Kompany was one of the three candidates on the last shortlist he had drawn up.

“I then asked him one final question: ‘Do you believe he can coach Bayern Munich?’ He said, ‘One hundred per cent. Absolutely.’”

The conversation helped convince Rummenigge that Kompany was the right man for the job. He subsequently shared Guardiola's assessment with the rest of Bayern's hierarchy.

“I told them I’d spoken to Pep. I’d never heard him speak so highly of another person as he did of Vincent Kompany. From his point of view, there was absolutely nothing to stop us offering him a contract,” he recalled.

Kompany went on to join Bayern in 2024, while Guardiola was succeeded by Enzo Maresca as Manchester City manager last summer.

#2338. Luc Chabert rêvait d'affronter les Verts

Coprésident du GFA Rumilly Vallières (N1), le réputé fromager Luc Chabert explique au Dauphiné Libéré pourquoi il est si content d'affronter les Verts demain après-midi à Annecy. Extraits.

"Mon père Gérard partait à Geoffroy-Guichard les soirs de Coupe d’Europe. Il était même présent à Glasgow en 1976, il est rentré 4 jours après ! On a toujours vécu avec le maillot vert à la maison. Mon père était président de l’ES Vallières, on jouait en vert. L’origine de la couleur du maillot, c’est l’ASSE. Donc, petit, j’ai baigné dans le vert entre l’ASSE et Vallières. Je crois que c’était la première fois que nous tombions dans le même chapeau que Saint-Étienne. Quand j’ai vu le groupe, j’ai envoyé un SMS à mon fils, Edgar, lui aussi supporter des Verts. Depuis le temps qu’on rêvait de jouer l’ASSE en Coupe de France, notre rêve s’est réalisé !

On a eu des super relations avec les dirigeants stéphanois pour l’organisation du match. Les planètes se sont alignées. Sans le FC Annecy, nous n’aurions pas pu organiser un tel rendez-vous. Et sans la complicité de l’ASSE, on n’aurait pas pu jouer le dimanche après-midi. Ils seront très bien accueillis. Le match, on va le jouer pour le gagner, c’est une certitude. Surtout, on va le vivre pleinement car on n’a aucune pression. On accueillera quoi qu’il arrive le résultat avec fierté et la satisfaction du travail bien fait. #2337. Dual passports issue continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND said the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

The Dutch football association KNVB launched an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser said it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

“Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”

Some players said they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius said he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

“I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that says I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”

#2336. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#2331. Feyenoord facing fireworks fine after 3-0 loss to Internazionale

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

Referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

One flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst said. “What do you do about that?”

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente said the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

“This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”

Van Bronckhorst said he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

“Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”

#2330. Joachim Löw impressed by Klopp's start as Germany boss but warns of setbacks

Joachim Löw has praised Jürgen Klopp for the start he has made as Germany head coach, having taken over from Julian Nagelsmann last summer following the disappointing World Cup round-of-32 exit against Paraguay.

“He is doing a very, very good job. He gives the players a lot of confidence and is trying to develop a sustainable playing philosophy. You get the feeling that things are heading in a positive direction,” Löw, who led Germany to World Cup glory in 2014, told Bild TV on Sunday.

Löw believes Klopp has already got plenty right, including his decision to name 44 players in his first squad and his handling of the controversy surrounding Felix Nmecha's religious crown celebration.

However, he also urged caution against raising expectations too high, with Germany having struggled to compete with the world's best since their World Cup triumph in 2014.

“His name alone does not always guarantee success. There will still be a few setbacks before we get back to that level,” Löw emphasised.

“The results are not all that important at this stage. We are in the Nations League now, and qualifying begins next year, which we will get through. The important thing will be for the team to spend six months playing together and building an understanding,” he said.

“You cannot expect any coach to get everything working within a few weeks. You have to look at whether there is progress,” Löw added.

Klopp and Germany will be hoping to secure a place in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals with a win over the Netherlands in their final Group A2 fixture on Monday.
